title: Pre-flight prints the same guider problem twice and both times tells you to connect PHD2, in a build that ships its own native guider
reasoning: Both halves are in the named file and the fix changes behaviour, not a label. equipment_rules.dart:105-148 builds per-node 'Guider Not Connected' warnings carrying affectedNodeId and only emits the generic 'No Guider Connected' summary when that list is empty, so the double count is gone. The description no longer names PHD2 ('${node.name} requires a guider but none is connected.') and the remediation goes through _guiderResolutionHint(GuiderState) at :190-204, computed once at :116 and shared by the per-node and fallback branches so they cannot drift. I checked the fixer's claims about OTHER files rather than trusting them: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/guiding/guiding_screen_parts/desktop_sections.dart:230 really does gate the Connect button on `!isConnected && isPhd2Guider`, and the else branch at :249-258 really does render an 'Equipment' button that calls context.go('/equipment'), so a non-PHD2 backend genuinely has no Connect button on the Guiding panel; isPhd2DeviceId is the shared canonical matcher in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/device_id.dart:267 and is the same predicate the Guiding panel uses, so the rule and the panel agree by construction. Not INCOMPLETE: grepping 'Connect to PHD2' / 'requires a guider' / 'Connect a guider' across packages+apps outside tests finds no second production site emitting this advice (the other hits are bridge API doc comments, a tutorial step, and two unrelated empty-state strings). Not DISCLOSURE-ONLY or RELOCATED: the string is now derived from state instead of hardcoded, and each branch names a panel that can actually do the job. Two honest caveats that do not unseat the verdict. (a) GuiderStateNotifier.setDisconnected() (guider_state_provider.dart) rebuilds `GuiderState(autoReconnect, lastError)` from scratch and therefore drops deviceId, so after a clean disconnect the rule takes the nothing-selected branch; the PHD2 and named-backend branches are reached from connecting/error states, i.e. the failed-auto-connect case the finding described. All three branches give correct advice, so no branch fails in the misleading direction. (b) Because `required` and the per-node loop are both derived from enabled nodes' requiredDevices, perNode can never actually be empty when required contains guider, so the 'No Guider Connected' fallback is effectively unreachable in production - harmless, and the shared hint means it would still be correct if reached. Whether the operator reads the right panel name on a real rig is not observable without hardware; every string is now state-derived, which is the strongest check available here.
evidence: Test 'missing-guider advice names the panel that can connect the selected backend' (packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_validation_ref_aware_test.dart:248-291) asserts all three branches, plus 'reports a missing guider once per affected node, with no duplicate summary' pins the de-duplication. SEVERED the production wiring: replaced `final hint = _guiderResolutionHint(gs);` at equipment_rules.dart:116 with the old literal 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' -> that test went red (00:00 +25 -1, all other 25 green); restored, and sequence_validation_ref_aware_test.dart + preflight_rules_test.dart both pass.

title: Node palette search ranks Smart Exposure above the node literally named 'Dither' when you search 'Dither'
reasoning: The third search box is genuinely on the shared ranker: sequence_tree_context_menu.dart:651 calls rankNodePaletteMatches(categories, _query) and the old `name.contains(q) || description.contains(q)` filter is gone; `filtered` feeds both the empty state and the ListView that renders the rows, so the ranking reaches the pixels rather than being computed and discarded. I hunted for a FOURTH surface, since covering three copies and missing one is this campaign's signature failure. There is none: every consumer of nodePaletteProvider is accounted for - widgets/node_palette.dart (mobile sheet + desktop sidebar, both fed by ONE filteredCategories computed at :60 and passed into _buildMobileSheetContent/_buildDesktopSidebarContent), sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35, this picker, and flatNodePaletteProvider -> sequencer_screen_parts/narrow_layout.dart:102, which is the narrow-desktop icon rail and contains no 'query'/'search'/'contains' token at all, so it has nothing to rank. snippet_palette.dart searches saved snippets, a different catalogue, not nodes. The picker's zero-result path renders NodePaletteEmptyState with a working Clear search, so the sibling empty-state defect is covered on this surface too. Behaviour change through a shared scorer, not a label change.
evidence: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart:442 'Insert picker ranks an exact name match above a description match' is a real WIRING test: it mounts SequenceTreeContextMenu, opens Insert Below, types 'dither' and compares getTopLeft(...).dy of the Dither and Smart Exposure rows. SEVERED by restoring the old unranked name||description filter (catalogue order preserved) at :651 -> that test went red (00:01 +11 -1) while the pure-function tests in sequencer_jank_p3_test.dart would have stayed green, which is exactly the signature that proves the wiring and not just the logic is covered; restored, and all 34 tests across sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart + sequencer_jank_p3_test.dart + node_palette_empty_state_test.dart pass.

title: Continue Session reports '0 minutes integration' for a session that has 12s of integration on the card behind it
reasoning: The named defect is genuinely fixed: quick_start_dialog.dart:138 is now `String _formatIntegration(double hours) => formatIntegrationHours(hours);`, the new packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/duration_format.dart rounds to whole seconds BEFORE splitting (so 59.6s reads '1m 0s', not '60s') and clamps non-finite/<=0 to '0s', and ParsedRunStats.formatDuration (sequence_stats_provider.dart:343) now delegates to the same function, so the Continue Session dialog and the dashboard/history run cards describe one run identically. I diffed the old formatDuration body and the swap is safe rather than a width regression: it produced the same h/m/s shape, differing only at rounding boundaries (old 3599.6s -> '59m 60s'; new -> '1h 0m 0s'), and nothing in either package asserts on its output. What does NOT hold is the claim's own cause-level framing - 'giving the app ONE integration formatter' - together with the fixer's explicit dismissal of the finding's named unit. They wrote that `screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart` 'is the wrong file'; that file contained the IDENTICAL bug (`_formatHours` did `(seconds / 60).round()` below one hour), so a 12-second carry-over rendered the sentence 'Carry-over: M13 has 0m from the most recent session (4 accepted frames)' - the same zero-beside-a-real-frame-count lie, in the file the finding pointed at. Opening that file, declaring it out of scope, and leaving the bug in it is INCOMPLETE rather than a mis-filed finding. It is now repaired (see repairSummary). Beyond that, the 'ONE formatter' claim is still false in this very area, and by more than the fix acknowledges: sequence_library_tab/sequence_card.dart:572 `_formatSecs` returns '0m' for anything under 30s, widgets/target_header_card.dart:601-602 and widgets/run_dashboard/target_header_panel.dart:351-352 both do `(secs / 60).round()` so a live short run reads '0m / 0m' next to its own frame counter, mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:1066 does the same in the resume banner, and quick_start_wizard_dialog.dart:1149 repeats it again. run_dashboard/target_header_panel.dart is the LIVE RUN header - arguably the most-watched of them - and was not in the fixer's account at all. I deliberately did not widen those five: they feed fixed-height Row/Column headers and cards that appear in capture-covered surfaces, and this campaign already produced a 24px Row overflow from exactly that kind of drive-by widening ('1h 30m 0s' is nearly twice the width of '90m'), so they belong in a change that can be golden-checked rather than in a verifier's confined repair. Recorded in blockedOnSharedCode.
evidence: Disclosure: a verify pass on this same shard ran earlier today and died before returning, leaving verdict-seqrun.json and this session_handoff repair already in the working tree; I re-derived every verdict from source rather than adopting that file, and I re-proved this repair by severing it myself. Repair present and pinned: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/session_handoff_dialog.dart:90 is `String _formatHours(double seconds) => formatIntegrationSeconds(seconds);`, and packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/session_handoff_dialog_test.dart:99-140 'a sub-minute carry-over is not reported as zero' pumps a 12s / 4-accepted-frame carry-over and asserts the tile text contains '12s', contains no '0m', and that the per-filter chip reads 'l: 12s'. SEVERED by restoring the old whole-minute _formatHours body verbatim -> that test went red (00:00 +2 -1) while the other three in the file stayed green; restored, and session_handoff_dialog_test.dart + quick_start_dialog_integration_format_test.dart + quick_start_dialog_honesty_test.dart all pass (13/13).
repairSummary: Session Handoff dialog's _formatHours now delegates to the shared formatIntegrationSeconds, so a sub-minute carry-over reads '12s' instead of '0m' beside its own accepted-frame count; regression test added that fails when the whole-minute rounding is restored. Five further whole-minute integration formatters in this area (sequence_card.dart:572, target_header_card.dart:601, run_dashboard/target_header_panel.dart:351, mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:1066, quick_start_wizard_dialog.dart:1149) left untouched and documented, because widening those strings changes Row widths on capture-covered and live-run surfaces.

title: A node can only be reordered by drag; the node context menu offers just Duplicate and Delete
reasoning: Every factual claim checks out against the source, including the ones about other files, and the git diff of sequence_tree_context_menu.dart confirms the fixer's account of what was already there versus what they added. Stale-inventory claim: TRUE - the pre-change menu already carried Skip to here, Insert Above, Insert Below, Duplicate, Group into Sequential, Group into Parallel, Disable/Enable and Delete, and the diff adds only moveUp/moveDown (entries at :245-256, enum members, dispatch cases, _moveSibling). False-comment claim: TRUE - kSequenceTreeShortcuts (sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart:64-71) binds Shift+ArrowUp/Down to TreeMoveSelectionUpIntent(extend: true) / TreeMoveSelectionDownIntent(extend: true), i.e. selection extension, and node_item.dart:857-858 now states that plainly ('binds Shift+Up/Down to EXTEND the selection, not to move a node - there is no keyboard reorder') rather than substituting a new invented claim. Shared-path claim: TRUE - _moveSibling (:479-502) calls currentSequenceProvider.notifier.moveNode(node.id, parentId, index +/- 1), the same entry point node_tree_view.dart:208 uses for the kebab and :93 for drag-drop. I checked the four ways this could be INVERTED and none fires. (a) The entries use the default `mutating: true`, so entry() sets lockedByExecution = !canEdit and greys them with 'Sequence is running - stop it first.'; a right-click cannot reorder a live run. (b) Index arithmetic is correct despite moveNode (tree_editing.dart:366-408) removing from the old parent BEFORE inserting: for [A,B,C], Move Down on B inserts at 2 into [A,C] -> [A,C,B], and Move Up on C inserts at 1 into [A,B] -> [A,C,B]; each is exactly one slot, and moveNode reindexes every sibling's orderIndex afterwards. (c) No null-assertion crash: moveDownDisabledReason evaluates `parent!` only after `rootOnlyDisabledReason ??` has been null AND `siblingIndex < 0` has been false, so root and orphan nodes short-circuit to a disabled entry instead of dereferencing a null parent; _moveSibling re-guards target<0/target>=length so a boundary move can never fall into a neighbouring container. (d) Disabled entries carry real tooltips ('Already the first node in its container.', 'This action is not available on the root sequence node.') rather than silently no-op-ing. This is added capability wired to real state, so it is neither DISCLOSURE-ONLY nor RELOCATED.
evidence: Three tests drive the real menu end to end in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart:361-434: 'Move Up shifts the node one slot earlier among its siblings', 'Move Down shifts the node one slot later among its siblings' (both long-press the row, tap the entry, then assert parent.childIds order in the provider), and 'Move Up is disabled on the first sibling and changes nothing'. SEVERED the production wiring by emptying the moveUp/moveDown cases in the dispatch switch (:342-346) -> both positive tests went red and the disabled-state test stayed green (00:01 +8 -2 with exactly those two named in 'Failing tests'), which is the correct signature: the tests fail on the CALL, not on logic inside _moveSibling. Restored, and the file's full 12-test suite is SUCCESS.
